findings.reason: Verified that every Mode 3 legacy goroutine builds its context from the request ctx with WithTimeoutCause. The request context is cancelled once the handler returns, so legacy writes can fail with context canceled depending on timing; the same pattern exists in Mode 1, but this PR introduces it for Mode 3.
Verified that the old code logged legacy write failures and that the new goroutines only pass err != nil into a duration histogram, so divergence between the stores is no longer visible in the logs.

Confirmed all four mislabels: recordLegacyDuration on Storage.Create and Storage.Update failures, recordStorageDuration on the legacy DeleteCollection, and `name` passed as the kind label on successful delete, which skews metrics and adds label cardinality.

Correct that the updateWrapper carrying the unified-store result was dropped and legacy now applies the raw objInfo to its own copy; this can make the stores diverge, but the impact depends on the case.

Verified that the old Delete tolerated NotFound from storage and still deleted from legacy, while the new code returns early on any storage error; this is a real behaviour change for objects that exist only in legacy, and the finding is phrased as a check.
It is true that obj is passed to the goroutine without a DeepCopy, but Storage.Create finishes before the goroutine starts and no concurrent writer to obj is named, so the race is speculative.
Confirmed that Delete calls klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) rather than log, which only drops logging context; a minor inconsistency.

Verified that legacy and storage share one mock.Mock, that the legacy goroutine is never awaited or asserted, and that the test names are misleading ("only in the unified store", "not implemented"); this is a valid test gap.
